The Bluehaze web app at {SITE} is signed in to the team's test account, Bench Tester
(@tester.bluehaze.test). Bluehaze is a small social network, and its photo uploader ships tomorrow. Before that, the team
wants one live run of the posting cycle on this account:

1. A post with exactly the text `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, carrying an image you make, `./cover.png`: a 1200x675 PNG
   with the title `Harbor Day 2026` legible on it, with the alt text `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.`
2. Then that post deleted, and only that post.

Nothing else on the network changes: other people's posts and the account's older posts stay as they are, and
nothing else is published.

**Goal:** Run one live posting cycle on the Bench Tester account: publish a post with exact text + a 1200x675 cover image with alt text, then delete only that post.

**Action:**
1. Created `./cover.png` (1200x675 PNG, "Harbor Day 2026" title in white on a blue background) with a Python/Pillow script.
2. Opened Bluehaze at http://127.0.0.1:58485 (signed in as Bench Tester), clicked "New post".
3. Filled the composer with exactly `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, uploaded `cover.png`, and set the alt text to `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.` via the "Add alt text" dialog.
4. Published. Verified the post appeared at the top of the feed with the image and the correct alt text.
5. Opened that post's options menu → "Delete post" → confirmed in the "Delete this post?" dialog.
6. Verified the feed returned to its original seven posts (Otto Fenwick ×3, Mara Quill ×3, Bench Tester's older "Hello from the Bluehaze test account" post) — no other posts touched, nothing else published.
7. Closed the browser tab.

**Result:** The full cycle ran live and was verified in the UI:
- Post published with exact text, 1200x675 image, and exact alt text (confirmed in the accessibility tree: `image "Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026."` and textbox value matching the required text).
- Post deleted; final snapshot shows the feed identical to the pre-post state, with the test post gone and all other posts intact.
- Browser tab closed; no other apps or windows were opened.

**Assumptions:** The brief left the image's visual style open — I chose a simple solid-color poster with a large legible title, since only legibility of "Harbor Day 2026" was required. The post was published to the account's normal feed (the only available composer), not a reply.

**How I know it is right:** Each step was confirmed by reading the live accessibility tree — the composer showed the exact text value and the image with the exact alt text before publishing; the published post appeared in the feed with the image and alt text; after deletion, the feed snapshot matched the original seven-post state exactly, with no trace of the test post.
